observed_original_abi.hidden_receiver: ECX holds a pointer to the subobject that carries the OnKeyDown virtual; the entry rewinds it to the cMouseCamera start
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: bool is the declared type carried by the SDK symbol (GhidraFunction.return_type = bool, return_type_resolved = true) and is the type the modelled source span declares. The machine never materialises a 0/1 AL: 0x007d9bb0 executes `MOV EAX,ESI` with ESI holding the receiver, so the full dword receiver pointer is returned. For a live object that value is non-zero, so the SDK bool observes `true` on every path. Modelled as `delegate(...) != nullptr`; no evidence fixes a false path.
observed_original_abi.ret_form: none in this body - the entry tail-jumps; the callee at 0x007d9bb0 ends with `POP ESI` / `RET 0x4`
observed_original_abi.receiver_use: ECX is the only register the entry touches: `SUB ECX,0x4` rewinds it by four bytes, and 0x007d9bb0 immediately copies it to ESI and uses it as the object pointer.
observed_original_abi.stack_frame: none; the entry pushes nothing and owns no cleanup. The one four-byte argument is popped by the callee's RET 0x4, so the effective caller-side stack effect is zero.

mechanics.classification: this-adjusting thunk (MSVC adjustor thunk), 8 bytes, no body
mechanics.why_minus_four: 0x007d93a0 installs three vtable pointers at +0x00 (0x014128a8), +0x04 (0x01412894) and +0x08 (0x01412890). The word stored at 0x01412894 is 0x007d9410, so this entry is slot 0 of the vtable of the +0x04 subobject and the incoming receiver is four bytes above the object start.

sibling_thunk.role: slot 0 of the vtable installed at +0x08 (word stored at 0x01412890); same shared implementation, -8 adjustment. The pair is what proves the -4 adjustment of the assigned target.

shared_implementation_007d9bb0.effect: Call the vtable rewriter 0x007d93a0 on the receiver; if bit 0 of the single four-byte argument is set, call 0x00f47380 with the receiver; return the receiver in EAX.

observed_sequence: MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x24]; if nonnull, MOV EAX,[ECX]; MOV EDX,[EAX+4]; CALL EDX - owner virtual slot +0x04 on the +0x24 pointer.
MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x8],0x13ef094; MOV dword ptr [ESI+0x4],0x13eb394; MOV dword ptr [ESI],0x13eb938 - the three stub vtable words.
vtable_rewriter_007d93a0.role_claim: not claimed. The sequence is modelled verbatim as rewrite_vtables_007d93a0; whether it is a constructor, an unload or a reset pass is unresolved.

deallocate_00f47380.convention: __cdecl, one four-byte argument, plain RET (caller-clean; the caller at 0x007d9bc5 does ADD ESP,0x4)
deallocate_00f47380.effect: Null-guard the object, then call 0x009276c0 with ECX = the global at 0x016c8b44 (labelled GeneralAllocator::sInstance) and the object as the argument.

allocator_remove_009276c0.argument: one four-byte object pointer on the stack
disassembly: MOV ESI,dword ptr [EDI + 0x4e4] - the allocator's lock word
PUSH ESI / CALL dword ptr [0x013cc2d8] / INC dword ptr [ESI + 0x18]
TEST ESI,ESI / JZ 0x009276f7 / DEC dword ptr [ESI + 0x18] / PUSH ESI / CALL dword ptr [0x013cc2dc]
allocator_remove_009276c0.effect: Scoped critical region around 0x00926fd0: enter through the IAT word at 0x013cc2d8 and bump the lock counter at +0x18, then leave through 0x013cc2dc after decrementing it. Modelled with the lock counter balanced to zero.

mechanics.bit_zero_gate: TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1 / JZ - only bit 0 of the single argument word selects the 0x00f47380 chain. With PUSH ESI active, [ESP + 0x8] is the argument at [ESP + 0x4]; the test is a byte test, so the upper three bytes of the argument are not examined.

call_graph.dispatch: virtual only; the sole reference to 0x007d9410 is the data word at 0x01412894

vtable_evidence.third_slot_word_unread: 0x671f5000 (the dword at 0x014128a8 is not a code address in this image; its identity is unresolved)
vtable_evidence.limit: The tables prove function-pointer storage, slot index and subobject displacement. They do not prove the class names of the three interfaces, the runtime registration of the tables, or that the pair of thunks is the complete OnKeyDown override set.
